title: Amend: fix the commit you just made
summary: Forgot a file, typo'd the message, committed on the wrong identity. Amend fixes all three — and quietly replaces the commit with a different one, which matters the moment it has been pushed.
mental_model: Amend does not edit a commit. Commits are immutable. It builds a brand-new commit from the same parent and moves the branch to it; the old one becomes unreferenced. That is why the sha changes.
danger: Amending a commit you have already pushed rewrites shared history. Your next push will be rejected, and forcing it will disrupt anyone who pulled.

steps.title: Survey the mess you just made
steps.why: The message has a typo, and the test file that belongs with this change was never staged. Both are one command away from being fixed — as long as nobody has pulled it.

steps.title: Write down the sha before you touch it
steps.why: Amend replaces the commit. Knowing the old sha lets you prove that afterwards, and lets you recover if you amend something you should not have.

steps.title: Fix just the message
steps.why: With nothing staged, `--amend` reuses the same tree and only rewrites the message. `-m` supplies it directly instead of opening an editor.
steps.expect: Same content, corrected message, and a different sha.

steps.title: Add the file you forgot
steps.why: Stage the missing file, then amend with `--no-edit` to keep the message untouched. The result is one clean commit instead of a follow-up called 'add missing test'.

verify.label: both files are in the one commit
verify.hint: git add dosing_test.py, then git commit --amend --no-edit

steps.title: Confirm the history is still two commits
steps.why: Three amends, still two commits. Amend never adds to history — it substitutes. Compare that with a 'fix typo' commit, which is permanent noise.

steps.title: See the commits you replaced
steps.why: The superseded commits are still in the object database, listed in the reflog. Nothing was destroyed; the branch simply stopped pointing at them.

verify.label: history is still two commits — amend substitutes, it does not append
verify.hint: use --amend rather than making a follow-up commit

verify.label: the typo in the message is gone
the forgotten test file is in the same commit

pitfalls: Amending a pushed commit means your next push is rejected. Use `--force-with-lease` only if you are certain nobody has pulled it.
`--amend` with staged changes folds them in silently. Always check `git diff --staged` first, or you will amend something unrelated.
`--amend --reset-author` also refreshes the author identity and timestamp — needed when you committed with the wrong email.
Amended the wrong thing? `git reset --hard <old-sha>` from the reflog puts it back exactly.
cheatsheet: fold staged changes in, keep the message
also refresh author identity and date
note the sha before you rewrite it
